2.name: text_block

0.name: block
0.value:
Turns each upper arm about vertical by an angle you set, holding the forearm and hand where they are in the world: the correction for an upper-arm sensor whose compass heading is wrong.

A magnetized sensor's heading error is not constant. It depends on which way the sensor faces, rising and falling once per turn of the dancer, so with the arm out to the side it shows as the arm sitting too far forward facing one way and too far back facing the other, and with the arm hanging it only twists the arm. Each arm gets that wave and a constant:

  swing    how large the once-per-turn error is, in degrees
  phase    the heading where it peaks, in degrees
  offset   a constant turn about vertical, in degrees

The angle applied is swing x sin(heading - phase) + offset, where heading is how far the upper arm's sensor is turned about vertical. Play a take where the dancer turns, with the arms out to the side, and dial each arm until it stops swinging forward and back as the dancer comes round.

It is for exploring by eye before learning. Swing and phase are exactly the correction shadow_mag_correct's yaw weights make: the 'yaw weights' outlet sends the 42 numbers with the yaw slots filled (everything else 0), to start t.param from. The offset has no counterpart in those weights.

SYNTAX:
shadow_heading_adjust

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

pose in:
Shadow quaternions, scalar first: one pose (37 or 20 joints, 4 each) or a take (frames, joints, 4). Numpy in gives numpy out.

adjust (checkbox, also an inlet):
Off passes the pose through untouched - for comparing.

left swing, left phase, left offset, right swing, right phase, right offset (float boxes, also inlets):
Degrees. Each change re-adjusts the pose already held, so a paused body follows the knobs.

OUTPUTS:

pose out:
The adjusted pose or take, in the layout it came in.

angles:
The angle each upper arm was turned, left then right, in degrees: two numbers for a pose, one pair per frame for a take.

yaw weights:
42 numbers for shadow_mag_correct's weights or t.param: swing and phase as its yaw weights.

READING THE DEMO:
At rest the sensor's heading is 0, so with swing 0 only the offset acts: 20 degrees turns the left upper arm about vertical. Click the button: the left_shoulder row of the angles shows the turn, and the left_elbow row the opposite, so the forearm stays where it was.

RELATED:
shadow_mag_correct carries the same correction as learnable yaw weights, with the hang, roll and forearm corrections; t.param and t.optimize learn them.
